items.body: Review by VianaProghead — Review N� 980Porcupine Tree is an English progressive rock band that was formed in 1987 in Hemel Hempstead, Hertfordshire. The band consists of a mix of prog rock, psych rock, avant-garde experimentalism and heavy metal. Despite this, Wilson doesn't have the same opinion. He mentions that Porcupine Tree's music is very simple, without complex elements. The complexity is in the production, in the way the albums are constructed. His first recordings "On The Sunday Of Life..." released in 1992 and "Up The Downstair" released in 1993, contain Wilson's first compositions, reminiscent of the cosmic rock of old glories like Pink Floyd and Eloy, but also resemble of the ambient rock from some contemporary bands like Ozric Tentacles. Wilson played all the instruments and did the drum programming. In addition, he invited some guest musicians to complete the picture on those works. By recording his acclaimed third album "The Sky Moves Sideways" released in 1995, which is the subject of this review, Wilson makes Porcupine Tree a true band. The new group received acclaim from critics around the world who describe the band as "The Pink Floyd of the new century".So, "The Sky Moves Sideways" is the third studio album of Porcupine Tree that was released in 1995. The line up on "The Sky Moves Sideways" is Steven Wilson (vocals, electric and acoustic guitars, bass guitar, keyboards, flute, tapes and programming), Richard Barbieri (keyboards and electronics), Colin Edwin (bass and double bass guitars) and Chris Maitland (drums and percussion). "The Sky Moves Sideways" had also the participation of Suzanne Barbieri (vocals), Theo Travis (flute), Gavin Harrison (drums overdubs) and Rick Edwards (percussion), all as guest musicians.After some success achieved with their previous albums, Wilson decided it was time for the band to hit the road, but for that he would have to have full-time musicians around. So he recruited the talented Richard Barbieri, Colin Edwin and Chris Maitland. Originally, the album should have been released as a single track, an epic work of about 50-minutes. However, this version was never finished, but divided into two parts which added up to about 36-minutes that begin and end the album, following an idea similar to that of Pink Floyd in "Wish You Were Here", with "Shine On You Crazy Diamond". In general, "The Sky Moves Sideways" walks in the footsteps of Pink Floyd, like no other work of the band, with a modern approach. With this work, the band manages to create a great album that picks up the tempo at the right places with rocky excursions where no boredom is and there's always something to discover even after many runs.The original version of "The Sky Moves Sideways" has six tracks. As I mentioned above, the title track suite is divided in two parts, opening and closing the original album. At its core, it was constructed and recorded alone by Wilson, but had overdubs by each of the three new members of the band, although Maitland didn't replace the drum machine, but only played the congas. The shortest recordings filling the middle of the album remained completely recorded solo. The piece is made in the best space rock style with the atmospheric sounds of Pink Floyd. The main passages are based on improvisations. Even so, the moods and sections are always well structured, making the music develop in an involving and dynamic way. As the suite winds toward its conclusion, some of the earlier instrumental themes are reprised. This suite is a masterpiece. "Dislocated Day" with its Oriental mood and melody is an excellent and very dark song, with a strong and emotive guitar riff that glides through the song in a very solid way. Solid are also the other instruments that energize the music with the maximum force. "The Moon Touches Your Shoulder" is a kind of an introspective ballad. It features beautiful acoustic guitar chords surrounded by lush keyboards and Wilson's airy vocals. The second half of the track is when things get more intense. Layers of sound introduce a kind of a guitar cacophony that settles down and carries us to the next track. "Prepare Yourself" is a very short instrumental featuring a good guitar work over an atmospheric keyboard and subtle bass drum beats. "Moonloop" seems to have been released in countless versions and lengths. It was created on completely different principles than the rest of the album. In the absence of Barbieri, and with the percussionist Edwards, the band entered the studio to record an improvisation eventually completing the repertoire of the album. It comes a bit close to the sound of the central piece with its expansive space rock passages.Conclusion: "The Sky Moves Sideways" is one of the albums to indicate to someone who doesn't know the band's work yet. On it, they actually performed as a band for the first time. The album represents a turning point in the band's work. Overall, "The Sky Moves Sideways" is an excellent example of the new psychedelic music style. This is probably, for me, the most atmospheric Porcupine Tree's album. "The Sky Moves Sideways" has a lot of moody, hypnotic and deep musical atmospheres. This is really an entertaining journey of discovery through Wilson's cosmos of sound. "The Sky Moves Sideways" is undoubtedly a masterpiece where each song is well arranged, well performed and well written.Prog is my Ferrari. Jem Godfrey (Frost*)

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — The third studio album from Norwegian band Seven Impale is definitely one of the long-awaitedprogressive rock releases of the decade, as it arrives seven years after their previous work'Contrapasso'. Seven Impale is a six-piece band that plays a pretty complex and theatrical style ofprogressive rock - their sound is heavily informed by the avant-garde rock scene as much as it is byclassic prog acts like Crimson and Van der Graaf. One could say their music is wilder than �nglag�rdand Ankedoten, yet it is no less sophisticated than the output of bands like Shamblemaths or Birdsand Buildings. Ideally, Seven Impale play a fusion-inspired modern rendition of retro prog; one thatis playful and dense, but also compositionally astute. And this is precisely what I admire abouttheir third album 'Summit' - a relentless record made up of four epics replete with tremendousmusical ideas, downright anxious instrumental sections, an interesting predisposition to dissonance,and an infectious energy.The titles of the four tracks suggest a mythological thread that underpins the concept of thisrecord. The epic nature of the music is then certainly befitting for such a conceptual thread, asthe four large pieces of heavy avant-prog deliver an in-your-face technicality mixed up with theband's pleasantly theatrical delivery. Lots of saxes and analog synths appear on this album, whichhas righteously reminded some listeners of Wobbler. But unlike their compatriots, Seven Impaleincorporate gnarly guitar riffs into their music, bringing in an almost sludgy feel to the heaviertracks. And this album certainly does not shy away from displaying pounding sections of heavy prog.All four compositions on 'Summit' are around the ten-minute mark, and their usual structure involvesan instrumental intro, followed by a swift transition into the main verse (and this is where themore intense or unusual ideas enter), leading up to a chorus that could be anything from cerebraland anthemic to crazy and surreal, after which an extended instrumental section brings thatexplosion of hectic ideas, complex interplay between the different instruments, and an overalleccentric feel. I cannot decide if I like 'Hunter' or 'Hydra' more, but the 13-minute album closer'Sisyphus' is up there with the best material on 'Summit', which to me is nothing short of astunning album. Highly recommended contemporary jazz-prog.

items.body: Review by Stefano61 — Forty six years passed between the celebrated 1972 debut of Reale Accademia di Musica and this second album, one of the longest gaps between two releases in the history of Italian rock.Guitarist Pericle Sponzilli, the sole returning member from the original lineup, reactivated the name in 2018 after being invited in September 2014 by organizer Guido Bellachioma to perform at the Progressivamente Free Festival alongside old companions from Fholks and acquaintances such as l'Uovo di Colombo, la Raccomandata con Ricevuta di Ritorno and Saint Just.Sponzilli took the decision partly because, in the intervening decades, other formations had used the historic Reale Accademia di Musica name for records that, in his view, did not represent the group's real legacy; Angeli Mutanti was conceived as what he considered the true second album of the band.Around him he assembled Fabio Liberatori, formerly of Stadio and a longtime collaborator of Lucio Dalla, on piano and keyboards, Erika Savastani, from Deserto Rosso, on vocals, Fabio Fraschini on bass, and Andy Bartolucci on drums, with guest guitarists Gianfranco Coletta, Nicola Di Staso and Fernando Fera contributing to individual tracks.Produced by Sponzilli and Liberatori themselves and released on the twenty eighth of February 2018 through M.P. & Records, in CD and in a limited edition of 300 white vinyl copies, the album carries artwork by Daniele Massimi built around a cover painting by Luciano Regoli, singer of La Raccomandata con Ricevuta di Ritorno, deliberately reviving the band's original 1972 logo while signalling a more contemporary sound.That contemporary sound is the record's defining choice. Angeli Mutanti bears almost no resemblance to the pastoral, mellotron soaked symphonic rock of the 1972 original. It favors instead compact, melody driven songwriting, warm ballads and soft rock textures, carried by the constant interplay between Sponzilli's raspy, characterful voice and Savastani's soulful, soaring one.Progressive elements surface less as extended instrumental workouts than as harmonic and structural details tucked inside otherwise accessible songs: unusual time signatures, brief but unmistakable echoes of Genesis, and orchestral flourishes that recall the golden age of Italian symphonic rock without ever trying to replicate it outright.The opening title track, Angeli Mutanti (Mutant angels), conjures in music and words a set of strange, nameless creatures that fly without wings or feathers, emotionally charged yet harmless, invisible demons without any plan. Musically it is a deceptively simple pop rock tune, lifted by light Hammond organ touches and unhurried, tasty guitar soloing.Alba (Dawn) follows in 5/4 time, its Genesis influenced writing plain to hear. The lyrics describe a metaphorical search for the rising sun and for a better day beyond time and space, a way out of a dark landscape built on lies, set against a bluesy tension and cold, Neo Prog style synthesizers.Johnny e Adele, a melancholic ballad featuring guest guitarist Gianfranco Coletta, paints a beautiful girl dancing on the beach to the notes of a guitar, and the dreams of the guitarist who loves her, colored throughout by warm Moog textures.Cosa nascondono le nuvole (What the clouds hide), with Nicola Di Staso guesting on guitar, opens with a knowing, cryptic echo of Genesis' Hairless Heart before settling into a dreamy, sleek pop rock groove that closes on a Mellotron laced outro clearly indebted to PFM, its words reaching toward far horizons.The Beat Goes On (come la canzone), featuring Fernando Fera on electric guitar, is the album's most straightforward moment, an elegant ballad built on soft, chiming guitar lines.Tempo (Time) turns toward more overtly progressive territory within the record's song based frame, its title alone signalling the preoccupation with time, memory and change that runs beneath even the album's most accessible melodies.A dritta San Salvador keeps the same balance of refined songwriting and understated instrumental interplay that defines the album's midsection, and has been singled out by Italian critics, alongside Io sono qui, Johnny e Adele, Cosa nascondono le nuvole and Tempo, for the sophistication of its trame, its narrative and musical weave.Una sola immagine (A single image), included only on the CD edition, stands apart for its authorship: the lyrics were written not by Sponzilli but by Nada Malanima, the celebrated Italian singer songwriter, lending the song a distinct voice within the album's otherwise unified lyrical perspective.Io sono qui (I am here), introduced by an almost solemn marching rhythm, is full of positive energy and describes an experience of daily rebirth guided by a sensei, a spiritual master whose words function like a chant to be followed in the morning light.The closing instrumental, La pista e il miraggio (The track and the mirage), mixes vintage sounds with exotic, almost cinematic atmospheres, arriving at symphonic passages that sit somewhere between PFM and Pink Floyd, and sending the album out on its most overtly progressive note.Angeli Mutanti was warmly received both in Italy and abroad, in Latin America, Japan, Korea, Canada and the Netherlands, and convinced even critics who had followed the historic Reale Accademia di Musica since the seventies, though a handful of more nostalgic voices wished for longer, more overtly progressive arrangements. Heard today, that same compactness feels less like a limitation and more like a deliberate choice.My judgment: 4 out of 5.Angeli Mutanti succeeds precisely because it does not try to be a sequel to the 1972 album in anything but name and spirit. It is instead a confident, contemporary record built on strong songwriting, a well balanced male and female vocal partnership, and just enough progressive character, in its harmonies, its guest guitar work, its unexpected time signatures, to remind the listener exactly which tradition it comes from.For anyone building a collection around the Italian progressive rock scene and its long, often improbable afterlives, this is a genuinely excellent addition, and a fitting first chapter to the story that Sponzilli would go on to continue four years later with Lame di Luce.

This powerfulinterplay of feelings sets the tone for the entire album. The second track, "Avenge Not Yourselves",immerses listeners in an atmosphere of austere contemplation. Its slow, meditative melodies inviteintrospection, preparing the audience for the album's subsequent explorations. This meditationseamlessly transitions into "To Direct Your Hearts into Love", a piece characterized by itssoothing, tranquil tones. As one of the album's standout gems, it radiates warmth and evokes a senseof gentle elevation. Among the most memorable tracks is "I Feel Shine of the Day", inspired by apoem by Ekaterina Vorotnikova. This bright and enchanting composition conjures an almost fairy-tale-like atmosphere, reminiscent of a dialogue between mythical beings?perhaps a fairy and a unicorn. Itbeckons listeners to embark on a magical adventure of life, celebrating the beauty and wonder ofexistence. Building on the theme of benevolent and mystical beings, the album explores the conceptof unseen helpers and miraculous saviors. The track "For Them Who Shall be Heirs of Salvation"reflects on the idea of angelic intervention. Its title alludes to the divine mission of beings sentto aid the heirs of salvation. Through its intricate melodies, the piece suggests that by reaching toward theinvisible, we may touch something eternal and profound. items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — 2026 is the year of surprise-releases, and Boards of Canada definitely surprised their fanbase withthe release of a fifth studio album titled 'Inferno' on May 29, some thirteen years after'Tomorrow's Harvest'. The electronic duo consisting of Mike Sandison and Marcus Eoin has relied oncryptic messaging and atmospheric soundscapes ever since the 1998 release of their game-changing IDMcollection 'Music Has the Right to Children', and while this kind of music has never had a universalappeal in the mainstream, it has an undeniable edge that attracts listeners from variousbackgrounds. Going back to 'Inferno', this album echoes beautifully the darker and nostalgic tonesof earlier BoC albums. Perhaps a reaction to everything surrounding us nowadays, this eighteen-trackcollection expands the sonic palette of the Scottish duo and impresses with impeccable productionand a myriad of contemporary sounds. At its core a bleak-sounding album, however, this cinematic andexpansive release offers several intriguing electronic pieces, while it preserves the enigmaticnature of the duo's classic compositions.And still, no matter how many times I play 'Inferno', one unfavorable aspect of it always resurfaces- the styles and influences covered here can and do feel somewhat scattered. Of course, themasterful embodying of various sounds tends to compensate for the intimidating abundance ofdifferent genres of electronic music featured here, but this is something that underwhelmed mypersonal listening experience. Of the eighteen tracks on 'Inferno', I tend to really enjoy abouthalf of them, mildly appreciate roughly a quarter, and easily skip the rest. For example, 'Prophecyat 1420 MHz' enters with a moving eastern-inspired intro, which is followed by a haunting palette ofsounds that almost has a noir aesthetic to it. This darker aesthetic is then expanded on 'HydrogenHelium Lithium Leviathan', where the synths seemingly feed off each other, and on 'Somewhere RightNow in the Future', which reminds me of a gloomy daydream. 'Blood in the Labyrinth' is another trackexploring this somber atmosphere, and for whatever reason it reminds me of The Cure. At the sametime, the most intriguing pieces on 'Inferno' are the more ominous, occult-ridden tracks like'Father and Son' with its claustrophobic sound design, 'Naraka' and its wonderful tribal vibes, andthe uneasy but meditative piece 'The Word Becomes Flesh'.There are also many ambient-inspired instrumentals as well, and while some of them are lush andspacey, others feel like interludes or simply random entries. 'All Reason Departs' and 'MemoryDeath' are among the fine ones, while tracks like 'Arena Americanada', 'Into the Magic Land', and'You Retreat in Time and Space' strike me as forgettable. Overall, 'Inferno' is an excellentsurprise from Boards of Canada, and an album worthy of praise that offers a mostly alternativerendition of contemporary electronic music.

Born Keith Blake in Kingston in 1950, he made his name with Bertram Brown‘s Freedom Sounds label, cutting “Stone” over a King Tubby dub mix and following it with “Bucket Bottom“. That same open-throated, declamatory delivery runs through this one too, and the title leans on the old Psalm line about God as a rock. The riddim is the work of Hal C, the Alicante producer Mario Coloma, who came up through the Barcelona reggae scene and now runs Piramid Records. He laid the track down at his own studio, then brought in players from across the map to finish it. Karl Wright cut the drums in the United States, Roberto Sánchez handled the backing vocals at his A-Lone Ark Muzik Studio in Santander, and Danny Trees mixed and mastered. It lands as the label’s fourth 7″, a black-vinyl 45 in a full-colour sleeve, with a dub of the rhythm on the flip. items.body: I’M NOT SURE IF THIS WORLD SURVIVES I CAN’T TELL YOU WHAT’S TRUTH OR LIES IT DOESN’T MATTER IF YOU’RE LEFT OR RIGHT WE’RE ALL DEAD UNLESS WE ALL UNITE After more than four decades spent turning political disgust, technological dread, and distorted guitars into blunt-force industrial rock, Ministry is preparing to shut down the machinery. Al Jourgensen has announced that the band’s forthcoming album, Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery), will be its last, bringing one of heavy music’s loudest and most unruly careers to a close on October 30 through Cleopatra Records. The first preview comes with Burned Out, a new single accompanied by a video directed by Joshua Bradford, formerly of Revolting Cocks. The title sounds like both a diagnosis and a resignation letter, which feels appropriate for a band that has spent decades staring directly at American power, institutional rot, religious hypocrisy, corporate greed, and the people who profit from keeping everyone exhausted and furious. Jourgensen has rarely been shy about announcing exactly what he thinks of the world, and Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery) gives him one final album-sized opportunity to unload. The record finds Ministry taking stock of those in charge, the damage they have caused, and whatever possibility remains for people trying to move forward together without surrendering their minds in the process. Jourgensen is equally direct about his decision to end the band. “I’m fucking done,” he says. “I’m proud of what I’ve accomplished. I’m amazed at the path that it’s taken, from With Sympathy to where we’re at today, and all points in between. It’s been quite a ride, but I’m completely at peace with the fact that it’s done. It’s time to herd goats.” It is a characteristically Jourgensen farewell. Ministry’s history has never followed a clean route, moving from the synth-pop framework of With Sympathy toward increasingly abrasive combinations of industrial electronics, metal, punk, samples, drum machines, and political invective. Along the way, the group built a catalogue whose influence spread through alternative rock, industrial metal, electronic music, and nearly every basement club willing to risk its speaker system. Burned Out surveys a planet apparently being administered by arsonists, war profiteers, algorithmic creeps, petty tyrants, and terminally online lunatics, while everybody else stares into the smoke wondering which official lie they are supposed to swallow today. Wars multiply, humanitarian disasters become background noise, the climate cooks, repression spreads, and domestic extremism crawls out of the basement wearing a flag. Beneath all that wreckage sits one stubborn plea: stand together before fear, division, and authoritarian power finish carving us into manageable pieces. The video turns the crisis into a parade of deranged animation, with Uncle Al planted at its center like the last sane man at the end of civilization, coat practically on, ready to abandon the madhouse before somebody asks him to save it. Watch below: Since beginning in 1981, Ministry has released 17 studio albums, 8 live releases, 8 side projects, tours across 5 continents, an autobiography, 2 documentaries, and at least 3 occasions on which Jourgensen received last rites. The survival stories became inseparable from the music, turning the band’s continued existence into a running argument against medical probability and professional caution. Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery) also closes part of the Ministry story by reconnecting Jourgensen with longtime member Paul Barker. Barker appears on the album’s final track, We’re Still Here, marking one last collaboration between two musicians whose work together helped define Ministry’s most widely celebrated period. The album also features Ministry’s current lineup, including guitarists Monte Pittman and Cesar Soto, bassist Paul D’Amour, sampler and synthesizer player John Bechdel, and drummer Pepe Clarke Magaña. Together, they provide the final formation behind a band that has spent 45 years treating complacency as an enemy and volume as a public service. Ministry’s final album, Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery), is out October 30 through Cleopatra Records. Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery) will be available in several formats including vinyl, CD, cassettes and digital, also including several vinyl variants and box sets: Green & Black Splatter LP Silver & Black Splatter LP Coke Bottle Green LP Box Set: Green Splatter LP, Picture LP, 7-inch, CD Box Set: Purple Marble LP, Picture LP, 7-inch, CD Fans can pre-save the digital album HERE and pre-order digital copies HERE, and find a new Ministry merch line HERE. Ministry will bring tracks from Hate To Go (Take Out Or Delivery) and other classic hits on the road in 2027 with an international goodbye tour. The Goodbye Europe Tour, featuring special guest Die Krupps, begins in April 2027. It will be followed by a full U.S. run, to be announced. European tour dates will include exclusive meet-and-greet opportunities with Al Jourgensen, featuring a photo op, a souvenir laminate pass, a silk-screen poster, and a final European tour coin. Fans can purchase meet-and-greets here. In the meantime, Ministry has a few final U.S. tour dates for 2026, including Chicago’s Salt Shed, the historic Red Rocks in Colorado and appearances at Louder Than Life and Sick New World Texas. Find more info and tickets at MinistryBand.com. items.body: PUREST FORM’s latest single, ANIMAL, opens with electronic menace. A blunt industrial beat stomps into view, guitar slashes scrape across the machinery, and Story Beeson’s voice carries the command of somebody who has already located the emergency exit. The Los Angeles trio wanted “White Zombie meets Underworld,” which sounds on paper like a backstage argument at a 1997 festival, yet the combination proves remarkably natural. Beeson, guitarist and programmer Madi Woodward, and bassist Riley Oikawa-Dahlson bring hardcore discipline to music designed for bodies in motion. ANIMAL pivots between serrated riffs, fractured breakbeats, low-end pressure, and sudden structural swerves, but every turn feels purposeful. The track has muscle, sex, and a mean little grin. Its aggression never becomes gray sludge; there is too much rhythmic wit in the programming, too much snap in the bass, and too much pleasure in the collision between metal weight and acid-house momentum. There is also a refreshing lack of genre etiquette here; stylistic boundaries are treated as petty municipal ordinances, useful mainly for telling dull people where to stand, then barrel through them with the cheerful confidence of repeat offenders. Beeson’s performance supplies the volatile center. She delivers each line as though language has become a physical object requiring immediate disposal, shouting near the edge of collapse while retaining enough control to sharpen every phrase. Around her, Woodward’s guitar behaves less like decoration than a damaged power tool, while Oikawa-Dahlson keeps the track planted firmly enough for the electronics to lunge, buck, and misbehave. The video, directed by Beeson, extends the song’s argument into the realm of surveillance horror. “The video takes on the horror of surveillance,” says Beeson. “While using a lot of throwback technology, mostly to pay homage to its influence – Peter Christopherson’s video for Ministry’s Over The Shoulder, it very much intends to communicate how more modern technology is being used for violence against our communities and humanity as a whole. It fits with the concept of ANIMAL: whether the nature is sexual or simply a desire to exist, we deserve to have freedom and we must take that freedom back.” Watch the video for Animal below: That conviction also drives RESISTANCE, the six-track EP arriving September 4 through Dais Records. Written amid fires, displacement, ICE raids, and the grinding obscenity of late-stage capitalism, the record channels anger toward collective action rather than private despair. “Resistance, less of an idea, more of an absolute action that has to be taken,” asserts Beeson. ANIMAL makes that action feel immediate, physical, and dangerously enjoyable. Revolution may remain poorly organized, but PUREST FORM have at least supplied it with a better bassline. items.body: Once all the papers get signed We lift you up on discount price You just have to make this sacrifice Every false prophet and messiah begins by telling the frightened that they have been chosen. The voice offers clarity, belonging, and the promise of a perfected self; only later come the contract, the price, and the surrender of everything that made the convert difficult to own. On Sacrifice, Southeast London industrial post-punk project The Pixel Rain sends that transaction through the age of algorithmic gurus, where charisma can pass for truth and transformation becomes a product. Sacrifice is the second single and opening track from The Pixel Rain’s forthcoming debut album, A Sense of Danger, currently scheduled for release in late October. Following Last, the song introduces the album’s post-apocalyptic frame through a society governed by power, authority, consumerism, and technological control. Sacrifice moves through a cyberpunk dream of deep bass, Kraftwerkian retro-computer pulses, and synth leads glowing with the sterile polish of a showroom terminal. Áron Siegler’s dusky voice maintains a close, controlled pressure throughout the verses, then surges through the chorus’s “So trust me,” landing somewhere between Brian Molko, Trent Reznor, and Paul Banks. Driving rhythms and industrial textures keep the track pushing ahead as the promise at its center grows steadily more predatory. The lyrics borrow the soothing vocabulary of cults, motivational seminars, and influencer culture. The prophet addresses his followers as “children,” while the parenthetical responses—“We’ll hold you” and “You know we leave no one behind”—resemble scripted affirmations designed to smother suspicion. A promise to remove self-doubt soon becomes permission to remove the self, with salvation reduced to paperwork, discount pricing, and the command, “You have to sell yourself tonight.” The final verse reveals what this digital saviour has wanted all along. “I prey on the void inside” turns an apparent confession of faith into an admission of appetite, before the closing line—“So we can eat you alive”—strips the sales pitch of its remaining benevolence. Siegler describes the false prophet behind the song: “‘Sacrifice’ started with the idea of modern-day false messiahs and how easily charisma can be mistaken for truth. As online platforms continue to blur the line between genuine guidance and performance, I found myself drawn to the psychology behind people who build influence by promising transformation. That idea felt like the perfect companion to the track’s cold, mechanical, electronic atmosphere.” The song’s science-fiction setting preceded its arrangement: “Like many of my songs, ‘Sacrifice’ started with a visual idea rather than a musical one. I was inspired by the worlds of Neuromancer and Cyberpunk 2077, and that atmosphere naturally led to a synth-heavy sound. From there, I mixed melodic influences from bands like Depeche Mode and Muse with the industrial pulse and textures of Nine Inch Nails and Ministry.” Created by Ádám Molnár, the accompanying lyric visualizer treats the viewer’s screen as the target of a computer virus. A digitized version of Siegler’s head becomes the infection’s persuasive face, addressing the viewer as the virtual machinery draws them further into its illusion. The polished interface connects the song’s false promises to the screens through which those promises now spread. Watch the visualizer for Sacrifice below: Sacrifice by The Pixel Rain is out via Bandcamp, Spotify, and all major digital platforms. A Sense of Danger is currently scheduled for release in late October. Listen to Sacrifice below, and order the single here. Sacrifice by The Pixel Rain Founded by Hungarian-born vocalist and multi-instrumentalist Áron Siegler, The Pixel Rain took shape within Southeast London’s underground and released a self-titled debut EP in 2023. Drawing from industrial rock, post-punk, synth-pop, and electronic music, Siegler balances guitar-led songwriting with layered production, dark atmospheres, and sharply defined melodies. A Sense of Danger extends that approach across songs concerned with power, authority, consumerism, and social unease, viewed through post-apocalyptic imagery and cold electronic machinery. items.body: Siouxsie and the Banshees released their third studio album, “Kaleidoscope,” on 1 August 1980 through Polydor Records. The album turns 46 this year. It arrived with a new lineup, drummer Budgie and guitarist John McGeoch replacing Kenny Morris and John McKay, who had abruptly left during the “Join Hands” tour, and it introduced synthesizers and drum machines to the band’s sound for the first time. The band recorded “Kaleidoscope” at Surrey Sound Studios in Leatherhead, the Coach House in Monmouth and Polydor Studios in London between January and May 1980, produced by Nigel Gray with Siouxsie and the Banshees. Siouxsie Sioux handled vocals along with guitar and synthesizer parts, Steven Severin played bass, guitar and synthesizer, and Budgie played drums and percussion; McGeoch contributed guitar, saxophone and keys, and Steve Jones added guitar on several tracks. The eleven-track album runs “Happy House,” “Tenant,” “Trophy,” “Hybrid,” “Clockface,” “Lunar Camel,” “Christine,” “Desert Kisses,” “Red Light,” “Paradise Place” and “Skin,” and was preceded by the singles “Happy House” and “Christine.” “Kaleidoscope” reached number 5 on the UK Albums Chart, the band’s highest chart position, and was later certified silver by the BPI. It streams on Spotify. About Siouxsie and the Banshees Siouxsie and the Banshees formed in London in 1976, when vocalist Siouxsie Sioux and bassist Steven Severin, part of the group of Sex Pistols followers known as the Bromley Contingent, put together an impromptu band to fill a slot at the 100 Club Punk Festival on 20 September 1976, playing a 20-minute improvisation with Marco Pirroni on guitar and Sid Vicious on drums. A settled lineup formed around Siouxsie, Severin, guitarist John McKay and drummer Kenny Morris, and Polydor signed the band in June 1978 after the single “Hong Kong Garden” reached the UK top ten. The band’s debut album, “The Scream,” followed on 13 November 1978, and “Join Hands” arrived in 1979. Two days into the tour for “Join Hands,” McKay and Morris abruptly left the band, and Siouxsie and the Banshees regrouped around new guitarist John McGeoch, formerly of Magazine, and new drummer Budgie, formerly of the Slits. This lineup of Siouxsie, Severin, McGeoch and Budgie recorded and released “Kaleidoscope” on 1 August 1980 through Polydor, reaching number 5 on the UK Albums Chart. The band followed it with “Juju” in 1981, which included the single “Spellbound,” and “A Kiss in the Dreamhouse” in 1982. McGeoch left the band in 1982, and the Cure’s Robert Smith joined as guitarist for the “A Kiss in the Dreamhouse” tour and the following two albums; John Valentine Carruthers then took over guitar for “Hyaena” (1984) and “Tinderbox” (1986), and the band released the covers album “Through the Looking Glass” in 1987. Guitarist Jon Klein joined for “Peepshow” (1988), which produced the US breakthrough single “Peek-a-Boo.” After a break during which Siouxsie and Budgie recorded as the Creatures, the band returned with “Superstition” (1991), led by the US hit single “Kiss Them for Me,” and toured as second headliners on the first Lollapalooza. “The Rapture,” produced with John Cale, followed in 1995 before Siouxsie and the Banshees disbanded in April 1996. “Kaleidoscope,” the album that introduced the McGeoch and Budgie-era lineup and the band’s electronic turn, turns 46 this year.

items.body: Suicide Commando, the Belgian electro-industrial project of Johan Van Roy, released its debut album Critical Stage on 1 August 1994 through the German label Off Beat. The CD turns 32 this year. The Suicide Sessions 1 (Critical Stage) by Suicide Commando “Critical Stage” contains 12 tracks, all written and performed by Van Roy, recorded and mixed by Eric Van Wonterghem at E.M.P.-studio. Cover design and layout came from Beyond > Mixed Data and Koen Cant. Track ten, “Where Do We Go From Here?”, carries voice and lyrics by Dirk Ivens, known from Dive, The Klinik and Absolute Body Control. Off Beat, a division of the German company Westcom, distributed the album through SPV GmbH. The original CD is out of print. The album can be streamed today via Bandcamp as part of “The Suicide Sessions 1 (Critical Stage)”, a 2011 reissue that restores the original twelve tracks alongside eleven bonus recordings. Out Of Line reissued “Critical Stage” separately on limited red and yellow vinyl in 2025. About Suicide Commando Johan Van Roy started experimenting with electronic music in Belgium in 1986 under the name Suicide Commando. His first tape followed two years later, and a track from it appeared on the vinyl compilation “Electronic.” After several more self-released tapes, Off Beat signed Van Roy, and Suicide Commando’s debut album, “Critical Stage,” followed in 1994. A second album, “Stored Images,” arrived in 1995 and included “See You in Hell.” In 1996, Van Roy marked the project’s tenth anniversary with the compilation “Contamination.” “Construct-Destruct” and its companion release “Reconstruction” followed in 1998, carrying the club tracks “Desire” and “Better Off Dead.” Van Roy co-founded the label Dependent in 1999. Suicide Commando’s next studio album, “Mindstrip” (2000), reached number one on the German Alternative Charts and was licensed for North America by Metropolis Records. Dependent also released the singles “Hellraiser” and “Comatose Delusion,” the EP “Love Breeds Suicide,” and the 2002 compilation “Anthology.” The 2003 album “Axis of Evil” was voted album of the year by the Deutsche Alternative Charts. “Bind, Torture, Kill” followed in 2006, preceded by the single “Godsend + Menschenfresser,” and reached number one on the DAC albums chart. Suicide Commando marked its 20th anniversary in 2007 with the “X20” boxset, including a remix disc, a “best of” disc, the “Fuck You Bitch” EP and the project’s first live DVD. In 2009, Van Roy signed with the German label Out Of Line, starting with the 7″ “Severed Head / Until We Die.” The album “Implements of Hell” followed in 2010, again licensed to Metropolis Records in the US. In 2011, Suicide Commando reissued its first three studio albums, “Critical Stage,” “Stored Images” and “Construct-Destruct,” as the six-CD box “The Suicide Sessions,” each remastered and paired with a disc of bonus and previously unreleased material. “When Evil Speaks” followed in 2013, led by the single “Attention Whore” and reaching number 47 on the German Media Control Charts. “Forest of the Impaled” (2017) included “The Pain That You Like,” a single featuring Jean-Luc De Meyer of Front 242 as guest vocalist, and reached number 28 on the same chart. Suicide Commando released the album “Goddestruktor” in 2022. For live shows, Van Roy performs alongside Torben Schmidt on keyboards and Mario Vaerewijck on drums. “Critical Stage,” the album that started the project’s studio discography, turns 32 on 1 August.

items.body: Los Angeles dance-punk trio Purest Form has signed to Dais Records. The label will release the band’s second EP, “RESISTANCE”, on September 4, 2026, and Purest Form has shared a video for the opening track, “Animal.” Purest Form is Story Beeson (vocals), Madi Woodward (guitar, programming) and Riley Oikawa-Dahlson (bass). The trio formed in Los Angeles in 2023 and draws on members’ backgrounds in hardcore bands alongside a shared interest in industrial and techno production. RESISTANCE by Purest Form “RESISTANCE” runs six tracks: “Animal,” “Break,” “Beyond Terror,” “More,” “Bass Resistance” and “Breathe.” The EP closes with a cover of The Prodigy’s “Breathe,” a song the band has performed live. Recording took place across 2025 with longtime collaborator and producer Andrew Oswald. The release is confirmed on CD and 12″ vinyl, including a black smoke vinyl variant. Video for ‘Animal’ addresses surveillance technology Beeson directed the video for “Animal,” the EP’s opening track. The video uses older recording technology to address the use of modern surveillance tools against communities. Woodward describes the direction behind “RESISTANCE” as a deliberate widening of the band’s sound: “We decided to just take it to the next level with this one. It’s like a unification of all the music that we love and feel. And it makes sense to us. If it sounds good, we don’t care where it comes from.” Beeson connects the EP to events in Los Angeles during 2025: “The nature and actions of our country are overwhelming, I can’t get away from the feeling of ‘what can we do to resist this at all costs?’ We have very radical fantasies across the board, making music that isn’t talking about what’s happening right now just feels unimportant to us.” About Purest Form Purest Form formed in Los Angeles in 2023, when Woodward and Beeson met while working at an independent venue in the city and bonded over a shared interest in underground music. Beeson also performs with Choking on Ash and Vacant Future, Woodward with Fury and Object of Affection, and Oikawa-Dahlson with Roman Candles and Pocketknife. The band released a self-titled debut EP in 2024, a set built around heavy, distorted guitar and programmed percussion. “RESISTANCE,” out September 4, 2026, is Purest Form’s second EP and its first release for Dais Records, recorded during 2025 with producer Andrew Oswald and led by the single “Animal.”

items.body: Hungarian artist István Gazdag has built a solid reputation within the EBM scene through his primary project, First Aid 4 Souls. A true workaholic, he is also active with side projects such as First Aid Tech. Two years ago, he released the outstanding debut album “Tech Under Your Skin” under this moniker. That impressive work is now followed by a new release featuring—once again—no fewer than 22 tracks. The influences remain largely unchanged. István Gazdag continues to experiment freely with a wide range of styles, moving from EBM—inevitably inviting comparisons to Front Line Assembly—to Tribal and Psy-Trance elements that occasionally evoke the spirit of Juno Reactor. Acid sequences emerge throughout the album, while guitar passages provide yet another subtle nod to the latter’s signature sound. Despite these obvious influences, First Aid Tech never comes across as derivative. Instead, the music feels like a seamless fusion of the various styles this sound guru effortlessly combines. There are no vocals, although carefully selected samples add extra depth and variety. The tracks frequently exude a menacing atmosphere that perfectly complements the album’s dark overall mood. Once again, Gazdag delivers a meticulously crafted production that merges boundless creativity with sophisticated, high-tech production values. To my ears, this new opus plays like the imaginary soundtrack to a “Matrix”-esque film. Above all, however, it stands as a brilliant, elaborate, and deeply immersive obscure Electro production. (Rating:8½). Listen to “Play My Game”: Play My Game by First Aid Tech About First Aid Tech First Aid Tech is a project of Hungarian electronic musician István Gazdag, who is also the driving force behind First Aid 4 Souls and Stahlgeist. First Aid 4 Souls, active since 2007, is known for its blend of industrial, EBM, dark ambient, trance, and new wave, often featuring guest vocalists. Stahlgeist deals in EBM that recalls the early years of Front Line Assembly and Wumpscut. Gazdag has performed and DJed under the First Aid Tech moniker for years, but the project’s first official release, a self-titled techno body EP featuring 4 tracks and 4 bonus remixes, only appeared on Alfa Matrix on December 4, 2023. The debut album, “Tech Under Your Skin,” followed on October 17, 2024. In a Side-Line interview, Gazdag described First Aid Tech’s sound DNA as rooted in 90s electronic music, citing Cabaret Voltaire, Orbital, Yello, Juno Reactor, LFO, Underworld, Empirion, and Future Sound Of London as reference points. The project now returns with its second full-length, “Back To Agartha.”

岡田尊司氏の提唱する克服の枠組み━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━日本語圏で回避型愛着障害について語られる際に最も広く参照されている岡田尊司氏の著書「愛着障害~子ども時代を引きずる人々~」(光文社新書)では、大きく3つの方向性が示されています。(1)子ども時代の未消化な体験に向き合い直すことつらかった記憶を抑え込むことで生き延びてきたぶん、その記憶を思い出し、言葉にして外に出していく過程が回復の入り口になるという考え方です。感情が言語化される過程では、最初は断片的にしか思い出せなかったものが、徐々に具体的な感情を伴って蘇ってくるとされ、その中で一時的に子どもっぽい甘えやわがままが表に出てくることもあるが、それは悪化ではなく回復のプロセスの一部として捉えるべきだと説明されています。出典: https://note.com/kaihigatano_pan/n/n0281059808d5(書籍『愛着障害』岡田尊司著の要約紹介記事)(2)他者を信頼し、受け入れ直す練習をすること自分が他者に受け入れられていないと感じる背景には、自分自身が他者を十分に受け入れていないことが関係しているという視点です。何でも話せる相手を見つけ、小さなことでもいいので誰かの役に立つ経験を積み、逆に誰かを支える立場に立つことも、信頼を築き直す助けになるとされています。(3)自分自身の中に「親」的な機能を育てること実の親からの影響に振り回されないよう、自分の中に落ち着いた「もう一人の自分(内なる親)」を育て、自暴自棄になりそうなときに自分自身を諭したり支えたりする、という考え方です。これは欧米の心理療法でいう「セルフ・リペアレンティング(自分を育て直す)」の概念と近いものです。出典: https://note.com/kaihigatano_pan/n/n0281059808d5━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━■3. 欧米の心理療法における具体的アプローチ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━セラピー分野では、回避型愛着に対して以下のようなアプローチが有効とされています。●アタッチメントベースドセラピー早期の愛着の傷に着目し、セラピストとの一貫した関係そのものを「修正的な体験」として活用する方法。出典: https://manhattanpsychotherapy.co/2025/09/14/moving-toward-connection-healing-avoidant-attachment/●感情焦点化療法(EFT)心理学者スー・ジョンソンが開発した、カップルセラピーの中でも特に実証研究が蓄積されている手法。パートナー間の愛着の傷そのものを扱う点で回避型に有効とされます。出典: https://positivity.org/mindfulness/attachment-styles-relationships●認知行動療法(CBT)「頼るのは弱さだ」「感情を見せると傷つく」といった、回避型特有の思考パターンそのものにアプローチする方法。出典: https://texascip.com/overcoming-avoidant-attachment-with-therapy/●精神力動的心理療法(長期)学術誌に掲載された症例報告では、回避性パーソナリティ障害を持つ女性が長期の精神力動的心理療法を通じて「獲得された安定型愛着」を築き、症状が寛解したケースが紹介されています。出典: https://psychiatryonline.org/doi/10.1176/appi.psychotherapy.2016.70.3.233●IFS(内的家族システム療法)回避的な態度や感情の遮断を「排除すべき欠陥」ではなく、かつて自分を守るために発達した「防衛的なパーツ(部分)」として捉え直すアプローチ。回避的な反応そのものと戦うのではなく、その反応がなぜ生まれたのかを理解し、優しく関わることで防衛が緩んでいくとされています。出典: https://www.embodyyou.ca/blog/healing-anxious-and-avoidant-attachment-with-somatic-therapy-ifs-parts-work出典: https://pasadenatraumatherapy.com/attachment-styles-parts-work-ifs-healing/●ソマティック(身体志向)セラピー・ポリヴェーガル理論に基づくアプローチ「安全」を頭で理解するだけでなく、身体で感じられるようにすることを目指す手法。トラウマは身体に記憶されるという前提から、グラウンディング技法や身体感覚への気づきを重視します。出典: https://growingbranches.net/healing-relational-wounds-from-avoidant-anxious-and-disorganized-attachment-to-felt-safety●EMDR(眼球運動による脱感作と再処理法)つらい記憶を圧倒されずに処理し、統合していくことを助ける手法として複数のセラピストブログで紹介されています。出典: https://www.karekounseling.com/blog/healing-the-avoidant-attachment-style●アイデアル・ペアレント・フィギュア(理想の親像)プロトコルIFSに近い発想を持つ、愛着修復のための専門的な技法として紹介されています。出典: https://maija-haavisto.medium.com/attachment-style-parts-and-internal-family-systems-3058f93bf72b━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━■4. 自分でできる日常的な練習━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━複数の情報源で共通して挙げられている、日常レベルで取り組める方法です。・感情の自己認識を高める:小さな感情も見逃さず、日々チェックインする習慣を持つ・ジャーナリング:関係の中で「近づいた瞬間」や「距離を置いた瞬間」を書き出し、パターンに気づく・脆弱性(バルネラビリティ)の練習:信頼できる相手に、小さなことから少しずつ本音を話す・身体感覚への気づき(ソマティックトラッキング):感情が体のどこにどう現れるかを観察する・自己への思いやり(セルフ・コンパッション):不安や引っ込み思案な反応が出たときに、自分を責めずに優しい言葉をかける・安定型の人との関わりを増やす:モデルケースとして学びながら、安心できる関係を体験として積み重ねる・境界線(バウンダリー)の練習:「ノー」と言うことも、健全な人間関係の一部だと学ぶ出典: https://bewelltherapygroup.org/2023/10/24/how-to-develop-secure-attachment-overcoming-avoidant-attachment-style/出典: https://psychology4u.net/psychology/how-to-heal-an-avoidant-attachment-style-a-psychology-based-guide/出典: https://www.karekounseling.com/blog/healing-the-avoidant-attachment-style日本語の情報源でも、日記などで感情を言葉にする作業が有効だとされており、「安全だと感じられる相手」と少しずつ感情を共有する経験を積み重ねることが、頼ることへの恐怖心を和らげると説明されています。焦らず自分のペースで取り組む姿勢が重要だという点が繰り返し強調されています。出典: https://katsushikabashi.jp/article/avoidant-attachment-style/━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━■5. パートナーや周囲の人ができるサポート━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━回避型本人だけでなく、周囲の人がどう接するかも克服のプロセスに影響します。・いきなり感情的な話題に踏み込まず、まずは論理的・具体的な会話から信頼関係を築く・共通の活動(例:週末どこに行くか一緒に決める)など、ストレスの少ない接点を作る・相手にとっての「安全基地」になる:安定した態度を保ち、批判的な言動を避ける・期待した反応がすぐに返ってこないことを想定し、寛容な態度で接する・相手の関心ごとに合わせて会話をすることで、信頼関係を築きやすくなる出典: https://atsu.theletter.jp/posts/02c2faa0-db54-11ee-af9e-ade4fb3034e5出典: https://mental.kashiwa-ekimae.com/34360/出典: https://tayama-counseling-office.com/%E5%9B%9E%E9%81%BF%E4%BE%9D%E5%AD%98%E3%83%BB%E5%9B%9E%E9%81%BF%E5%9E%8B%E6%84%9B%E7%9D%80%E3%82%B9%E3%82%BF%E3%82%A4%E3%83%AB%E3%81%AE%E4%BA%BA%E3%81%A8%E3%81%AE%E4%BB%98%E3%81%8D%E5%90%88%E3%81%84/学術研究でも、ポジティブな関係経験そのものが回避型愛着傾向を持つ人に恩恵をもたらすことが示されており、良い関係経験を重ねること自体が回避傾向を和らげる方向に働く可能性が示唆されています(Stanton, Campbell, & Pink, 2017, Journal of Personality and Social Psychology)。出典: https://light-clinic.com/what-is-avoidant-behavior/━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━■6. 注意点・現実的な見通し━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━・「治す」というより「傾向を緩める」というイメージの方が実態に近いとされています。回避型は障害というより関係性のパターンであり、不安やトラウマ歴と併存することはあっても、それ自体が精神疾患ではないという立場を取る専門家もいます出典: https://texascip.com/overcoming-avoidant-attachment-with-therapy/・変化は直線的ではなく、「気づき→実践→後退→また気づく」というらせん状のプロセスであると複数のセラピストが述べています出典: https://psychology4u.net/psychology/how-to-heal-an-avoidant-attachment-style-a-psychology-based-guide/・特に恐れ・回避型の場合は、神経系の調整(グラウンディングなど)により重点を置く必要があるとされ、単純な「距離を縮める練習」だけでは不十分な場合があります出典: https://psychology4u.net/psychology/how-to-heal-an-avoidant-attachment-style-a-psychology-based-guide/・セルフヘルプでの取り組みが難しいと感じる場合、専門的な心理療法(個人・カップルどちらも)が選択肢として推奨されています出典: https://www.brentwoodtherapycollective.com/blog/how-to-heal-an-avoidant-attachment-style-steps-to-build-secure-relationships━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━■まとめ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━回避型愛着の克服については、日本語圏では岡田尊司氏の「子ども心を取り戻す」「他者を受け入れる」「自分が自分の親になる」という3段階の枠組みが広く参照されています。一方、欧米の心理療法分野ではEFT・CBT・IFS・ソマティックセラピー・EMDRなど複数のエビデンスベースの手法が併用され、「洞察だけでなく、安全な経験の反復によって変わる」という点が共通して強調されています。続きをみる

items.excerpt: ■ 基本プロフィール本名リチャード・アルパート（Richard Alpert）。1931年4月6日、マサチューセッツ州ニュートンの裕福なユダヤ系家庭に誕生。父ジョージ・アルパートはボストンで有力な弁護士で、ニューヨーク・ニューヘブン・アンド・ハートフォード鉄道の社長を務め、ブランダイス大学とアルバート・アインシュタイン医学校の創立者の一人でもあった大物。3人兄弟の末っ子で、幼少期は「家族のマスコット」的存在として愛されて育つ。タフツ大学で学士号、ウェズリアン大学で修士号を取得後、1957年にスタンフォード大学で心理学博士号を取得（博士論文のテーマは「達成不安」）。その後ハーバード大学で心理学の助教授となり、社会関係学部・心理学部・大学院教育学部・保健サービス部門を渡り歩くエリート学者だった。メルセデスを乗り回し、カリブ海に別荘を持ち、自家用飛行機まで所有していたという。参照：https://www.inc.com/minda-zetlin/ram-dass-influenced-steve-jobs-be-here-now.html■ ハーバード時代とティモシー・リアリーとのサイケデリ
items.body: ■ 基本プロフィール本名リチャード・アルパート（Richard Alpert）。1931年4月6日、マサチューセッツ州ニュートンの裕福なユダヤ系家庭に誕生。父ジョージ・アルパートはボストンで有力な弁護士で、ニューヨーク・ニューヘブン・アンド・ハートフォード鉄道の社長を務め、ブランダイス大学とアルバート・アインシュタイン医学校の創立者の一人でもあった大物。3人兄弟の末っ子で、幼少期は「家族のマスコット」的存在として愛されて育つ。タフツ大学で学士号、ウェズリアン大学で修士号を取得後、1957年にスタンフォード大学で心理学博士号を取得（博士論文のテーマは「達成不安」）。その後ハーバード大学で心理学の助教授となり、社会関係学部・心理学部・大学院教育学部・保健サービス部門を渡り歩くエリート学者だった。メルセデスを乗り回し、カリブ海に別荘を持ち、自家用飛行機まで所有していたという。参照：https://www.inc.com/minda-zetlin/ram-dass-influenced-steve-jobs-be-here-now.html■ ハーバード時代とティモシー・リアリーとのサイケデリック研究1958年からハーバードで教え始め、1961年にはハーバード心理学部の同僚ティモシー・リアリーと出会う。二人はシロシビン（マジックマッシュルーム由来）やLSDを用いた意識研究「ハーバード・シロシビン・プロジェクト」に没頭し、自らも被験者として服用。ジャズミュージシャン、物理学者、哲学者、聖職者、麻薬常用者、大学院生など多様な被験者に薬物を投与し、体験後にアンケートを取るという手法を取った。1962年にはリアリーと共に非営利団体「国際内的自由連盟（IFIF）」をケンブリッジで共同設立し、宗教的文脈での向精神薬使用を研究。この研究は『チベット死者の書』を下敷きにした共著『The Psychedelic Experience』（リアリー、ラルフ・メツナーと共著）や『LSD』（シドニー・コーエン、ローレンス・シラーと共著）という書籍を生んだが、あまりに物議を醸したため、1963年、大学院生にもシロシビンを与えたことなどを理由にハーバードを解雇される（リアリーも無断で講義を休んだこと等を理由に同時解雇）。なお、リアリーの息子ジャック（当時15歳）を「誘惑しようとした」との告発もアルパートの死亡記事（NYT）に記されている。参照：https://www.ramdass.org/about-ram-dass/参照：https://matthewremski.com/wordpress/quotes-from-ram-dass-that-fit-the-pattern-of-spiritualizing-sexual-abuse-in-yoga/■ インドへの旅とニーム・カロリ・ババとの出会い1967年、アルパートはインドへ。旅の途中でネパールにて、アメリカ人の精神探求者バガヴァン・ダス（本名カーミット・マイケル・リッグス）と出会い、裸足で寺院を巡りながらマントラやアーサナ、数珠の使い方などの手ほどきを受ける。数ヶ月後、バガヴァン・ダスに導かれ、カインチ・アシュラムでヒンドゥー教の導師ニーム・カロリ・ババ（西洋では「マハラジ・ジ」として知られる）に出会う。伝説的なエピソードとして、アルパートが持参した大量のLSDをマハラジ・ジに服用させたところ、何の効果も表れなかった（少なくともアルパート自身はそう語っている）という逸話がある。マハラジ・ジはアルパートに「ラム・ダス（神の下僕）」という名を授け、これが彼の以後の人生を決定づけた。1968年に帰国。参照：https://allthatsinteresting.com/ram-dass参照：https://www.britannica.com/biography/Ram-Dass■ 『Be Here Now』（1971年）― ヒッピー世代のバイブル帰国後、心理学から瞑想やヨガ、東洋思想の伝道者へと転身。1971年に出版した『Be Here Now（ビー・ヒア・ナウ／心の扉をひらく本）』は自伝的要素とヒンドゥー教・仏教思想を融合させた内容で、カウンターカルチャー世代の聖典的存在となった。タイトルの「Be Here Now」は、旅の途中でバガヴァン・ダスが彼に繰り返しかけた言葉「過去のことは考えるな、ただ今ここにいろ」に由来するとされる。日本語版は平河出版社より刊行、訳者は上野圭一・吉福伸逸・スワミ・プレム・プラブッダ。参照：https://hirakawa-shuppan.co.jp/pickup/%E3%83%93%E3%83%BC%E3%83%BB%E3%83%92%E3%82%A2%E3%83%BB%E3%83%8A%E3%82%A6/参照：https://shopping.bookoff.co.jp/used/0015279360■ スティーブ・ジョブズとの関係『Be Here Now』はアップル創業者スティーブ・ジョブズの愛読書として広く知られる。1972年、リード大学に入学したばかりのジョブズはLSDを試しながら精神世界の本を読み漁っており、この本に強い影響を受けた。ジョブズ自身「profound（深遠）だった。自分や多くの友人を変容させた」と語ったと伝記作家ウォルター・アイザックソンの著作に記されている。ジョブズがインドへ渡った動機の一つも、この本の影響とされる。ラム・ダスはジョブズのほか、ザッカーバーグやラリー・ペイジなど後のIT業界のキーパーソンにも影響を与えたと言われる。参照：https://theceolibrary.com/be-here-now-636.html参照：https://tocana.jp/2019/12/post_134639_entry.html■ 慈善・社会活動1974年、非営利団体「ハヌマーン・ファウンデーション」を設立。傘下で刑務所を「僧院」に見立てて受刑者に瞑想を教える「プリズン・アシュラム・プロジェクト」（現ヒューマン・カインドネス・ファウンデーション、ボー＆シータ・ロゾフ夫妻が主導）や、死にゆく人々への意識的な向き合い方を支援する「ダイイング・プロジェクト」（スティーブン・レヴァインと構想、後にデイル・ボーグラムが主導する「Living/Dying Project」に発展）を展開。1978年には公衆衛生の専門家ラリー・ブリリアント、活動家ウェイヴィー・グレイヴィーらと共に「セヴァ・ファウンデーション」を共同設立。インド・ネパールなど途上国での失明予防・治療事業を行う国際保健団体として現在も活動中。ラム・ダスは著書の印税や講演料の多くをこうした団体に寄付し続けた。参照：https://www.hanumanmaui.org/ram-dass参照：https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seva_Foundation参照：https://www.ihanuman.com/journal/bolozoff/human-kindness-foundation-and-prison-ashram-project■ 1997年の脳卒中と「フィアース・グレイス（Fierce Grace）」1997年2月19日、自宅で一人でいる際に大規模な脳卒中を発症。右半身の麻痺と表出性失語症（言葉を発するのが困難になる症状）が残った。本人はこれを「stroked（打たれた）」と表現し、この経験を「fierce grace（苛烈な恩寵）」と呼んで、老いや死、苦しみへの向き合い方を再び深く見つめ直す契機とした。この時期の回復と変容を描いたドキュメンタリー『Ram Dass, Fierce Grace』（2001年、監督ミッキー・レムル）が制作され、Newsweek誌の2002年ノンフィクション映画トップ5にも選出。脳卒中の体験は著書『Still Here: Embracing Aging, Changing and Dying』（2000年、邦訳『死の処方箋
